deep.reconstruction:
Setting. U = P^1(C) - {0,1,∞} (= M_{0,4}) carries an action of Γ = S_3 × Z/2. S_3 is generated by the involutions σ̇_0 (z ↦ z/(z-1), fixing 0 and 2), σ̇_1 (z ↦ 1/z, fixing -1 and 1) and σ̇_∞ (z ↦ 1-z, fixing 1/2 and ∞), with ρ̇ = σ̇_0σ̇_1 of order 3 fixing P = e^{iπ/3} and P̄. Z/2 is generated by complex conjugation τ. Σ (called E on the previous page) is the group of all lifts of Γ to the universal cover of U. It is an extension 1 → π_1(U) → Σ → Γ → 1, i.e. the orbifold fundamental group of the real orbifold U/Γ. Forgetting τ, this is π_1^orb(U/S_3) = π_1^orb(M_{1,1}) ≅ PSL_2(Z); with τ it becomes the extended modular group PGL_2(Z).

What the page does. Grothendieck is systematically listing the conjugacy classes of finite (torsion) subgroups of Σ, or 'partial splittings', via fixed points of elements of Γ on U.
- The previous page handled the isolated fixed points 2, -1, 1/2 (renamed 0', 1', ∞'), with inertia groups {σ̇_i, τ} lifting to ⟨σ_i, τ_i⟩.
- It also handled the fixed locus of τ. U^τ = P^1(R) - {0,1,∞} has three arcs, each containing exactly one of 0', 1', ∞'. The corresponding conjugacy classes of lifts of {1,τ} are therefore those of τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞: nothing new.
- The remaining antiholomorphic involutions are τσ̇_1 and its ρ-conjugates τσ̇_0, τσ̇_∞. Since σ̇_1(z) = 1/z, we get (τσ̇_1)(z) = 1/z̄, with fixed locus {|z| = 1} - {1}, a single connected arc. It contains P, P̄ (and -1), so again it gives no new conjugacy classes of lifts; the lift is σ̃_1 = lift of σ̇_1τ.
- The implicit principle: conjugacy classes of order-2 lifts of an antiholomorphic involution correspond to connected components of its real locus (the archimedean section correspondence).

Then he turns to a presentation of Σ by generators and relations, starting from a presentation of Γ = S_3 × Z/2 and lifting generators judiciously. A first attempt is crossed out. It used generators ρ', τ and σ̃_i = σ̇_iτ, with ρ' = ρτ of order 6, ρ'^3 = τ, ρ'^2 = ρ^2 = ρ^{-1}, and relations σ̃_i^2 = 1, σ̃_0σ̃_1 = σ̃_1σ̃_∞ = σ̃_∞σ̃_0 = ρ, ρ'^6 = 1, ρ'^3 commuting with the σ̇_i. The next page replaces it by the presentation with σ_i, ρ, τ_i: σ_i^2 = τ_i^2 = ρ^3 = 1, ρ permuting the τ_i cyclically, τ_i commuting with σ_i, and σ_0σ_1 = τ_∞τ_1ρ, etc. The loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ appear as products of the τ's, with l_∞l_1l_0 = 1 automatic.

Purpose. This is the real ('Galois over R') structure of the genus-0, 4-point Teichmüller/modular group, part of the Longue Marche (1981) programme: discrete analogues of the Galois action and the anabelian/section philosophy at the archimedean place.
errors: No mathematical error in the computation: (τσ̇_1)(z) = conj(1/z) = 1/z̄, fixed set = unit circle minus {1}; it contains e^{±iπ/3} and -1. Since σ̇_1 has real coefficients, τσ̇_1 = σ̇_1τ, so writing σ̃_1 as the lift of σ̇_1τ is consistent.
The crossed-out presentation is incomplete and was rightly abandoned (e.g. it does not yet encode the free part π_1(U) or the l_∞l_1l_0 = 1 relation).

ideas.what: Classifying conjugacy classes of finite-order lifts of antiholomorphic involutions in the orbifold fundamental group via connected components of their fixed-point loci
ideas.modern_name: Real section conjecture / archimedean analogue of Grothendieck's section conjecture (components of X(R) ↔ conjugacy classes of sections of π_1(X/R) → Gal(C/R))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983, as a conjecture); proofs over R by Mochizuki, Pop, Wickelgren; exposition in Stix's book
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); Longue Marche (1981), where the real case is discussed

ideas.what: Computation of the extension of S_3 × Z/2 by π_1(P^1 - {0,1,∞}), i.e. the orbifold π_1 of M_{0,4}/(S_3 × conj) ≅ extended modular group PGL_2(Z)
ideas.modern_name: Extended (real) modular / Teichmüller group Γ_{0,4} ⋊ (S_3 × Z/2) ≅ PGL_2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Fricke); Grothendieck–Teichmüller framework: Esquisse, Drinfeld, Ihara
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche discuss T_{0,4}, T_{1,1} and the role of complex conjugation in general

ideas.what: Presentation of the extension by lifting a presentation of the finite quotient
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of group extensions / orbifold fundamental group presentation

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, correct worked example (real orbifold structure of M_{0,4}, lifts of antiholomorphic involutions) in the Longue Marche period. It illustrates the real section correspondence, but the results (PGL_2(Z), components of real loci ↔ conjugacy classes of involutive lifts) are classical or known, and the presentation attempt is crossed out.
transcription_corrections: 'ses conjugués par ρ τσ̇_0, τσ̇_0' should read 'τσ̇_0, τσ̇_∞'.
In the crossed-out block, 'ρ^{16} = 1' is 'ρ'^6 = 1' and 'ρ^{13} commute aux σ̇_i' is 'ρ'^3 commute aux σ̇_i' (prime plus exponent misread).
The line '(donc ρ'^6 = 1, ρ'^3 = τ, ρ'^2 = ρ^2 = ρ^{-1})' is correct as ρ' = ρτ.
The generators listed are ρ', τ, σ̃_0, σ̃_1, σ̃_∞, with σ̃_i lifting σ̇_iτ (written underneath).
'grands' is likely 'quatre' or a similar insertion, uncertain.
